aliases: Black Hills Industrial Center data center

location.site_description: Black Hills Industrial Center, south of Old Folsom Road and east of Highway 79; exact parcel/address not confirmed in accessible official records

status_as_of_cutoff: Local process / active proposal as of 2026-08-11. Elevate Rapid City published Sequitor Edge's 2026-02-11 announcement for a Tier 3 edge computing facility on approximately 10 acres in Rapid City's Black Hills Industrial Center. KOTA reported on 2026-07-02 that Sequitor Edge planned a 15 MW facility and that construction was not expected until late 2026; KOTA later reported on 2026-07-30 that residents raised oversight/CUP concerns at a city Legal and Finance Committee meeting, with no discussion or action by council members. No directly accessible Rapid City/Pennington project-specific zoning approval, building permit, construction, inspection, CO, Black Hills Energy interconnection, energization, commissioning, or service record was located. Earlier 2 MW initial / 10 MW expansion reporting remains in conflict with the later 15 MW report.
evidence_grade: Tier-2/Tier-3 local process evidence: Elevate Rapid City announcement, accessible local media reports, and indexed Rapid City agenda/permit pages; no accessible project-specific permit or utility-service record located.

actions.result_status: Elevate Rapid City published Sequitor Edge's announcement for a new Tier 3 edge computing center at the Black Hills Industrial Center, described as an approximately 10-acre greenfield facility creating three full-time positions. The announcement states Sequitor worked with local partners on site due diligence and utility-capacity alignment, but it is not a permit or approval record.
actions.access_caveat: Economic-development/partner announcement; no city approval is inferred.
actions.evidence_note: Confirms sponsor, approximate acreage, site, facility type, and jobs.

actions.result_status: Local reporting identified Sequitor Edge, the Black Hills Industrial Center site, a 2027 completion expectation, and permits still needed. The report is not a permit or approval record.
actions.access_caveat: Secondary local report; no zoning or building approval is inferred.

actions.result_status: Local television reported the Rapid City project was moving forward and described a 15 MW plan, while discussing local power constraints. No permit, interconnection, or construction milestone was provided.
actions.access_caveat: Secondary report; 15 MW is a reported plan and not a government-certified load.
actions.evidence_note: Reported project status kept separate from official utility evidence.

actions.government_body: Rapid City Legal and Finance Committee / KOTA-TV
actions.result_status: KOTA reported residents urged a Conditional Use Permit process and formal legal review for large-scale data centers during the Legal and Finance Committee meeting; the same report says no council members responded and no discussion or action on the proposed data center occurred.
actions.access_caveat: Local media report of a public meeting; no approval, denial, or permit action is inferred.
actions.evidence_note: Supports local-process status while preserving no-action caveat.

actions.result_status: Rapid City's public eTRAKiT portal exposes permit-search functionality, but access to permit search required login during this review. Search-index results also identified 26OA006 / Ordinance 6746 concerning definitions for micro, large-scale, and hyperscale data centers, but the direct City agenda-item page returned a Cloudflare 403 to this review environment. No accessible project-specific permit approval was confirmed.
actions.access_caveat: Official permit portal accessible only to the homepage/login flow from this environment; indexed ordinance page could not be opened directly.
actions.evidence_note: Negative/limited official-records check; does not prove no filing exists.

contradictions.summary: KOTA's 2026-07-02 report states Sequitor Edge plans a 15 MW facility, while KOTA's 2026-07-30 report says company officials had previously described approximately 2 MW initial use with expansion to 10 MW. Elevate Rapid City's 2026-02-11 announcement does not disclose MW. The data center tracker Server Country treats 15 MW as the current planned capacity and explicitly notes the earlier 2 MW / 10 MW figures.

history.reason: Later KOTA report and Server Country tracker identify 15 MW as current reported plan; conflict with earlier 2 MW / 10 MW reporting retained in contradictions.
Elevate Rapid City announcement and subsequent local reports identify Sequitor Edge as the sponsor/developer.
